definition: Alloformation is an allostratigraphic unit of Rank 4. Allostratigraphy (defining and identifying strata on the basis of their bounding discontinuities) is not normally used by BGS as a method of classifying lithostratigraphic units.

Allogroup is an allostratigraphic unit of Rank 2. Allostratigraphy (defining and identifying strata on the basis of their bounding discontinuities) is not normally used by BGS as a method of classifying lithostratigraphic units.

Allomember is an allostratigraphic unit of Rank 5. Allostratigraphy (defining and identifying strata on the basis of their bounding discontinuities) is not normally used by BGS as a method of classifying lithostratigraphic units.

Assemblage is a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 2 uniting two or more tectono-metamorphic units that are of lower rank and display a natural association. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.).

Bed is the smallest formal unit in the hierarchy of sedimentary lithostratigraphical units. Bed names are commonly applied to distinctive units that may be thin and laterally restricted or known only from a borehole or single exposure. Some beds may be fossiliferous or yield dateable material (e.g. a soil, peat or bone bed). Bed status tends to be assigned for units with some palaeogeographical, geochronological or specific lithological significance. This term forms part of the internationally accepted framework for classifying lithostratigraphical units, and has Rank 6 (McMillan, A A, Hamblin, R J O and Merritt, J W. 2011. A lithostratigraphical framework for onshore Quaternary and Neogene (Tertiary) superficial deposits of Great Britain and the Isle of Man. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/10/03. 343pp.).

Block is a volume of rock bounded by broadly rectilinear surfaces of tectonic or uncertain origin; also a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 6 with these characteristics. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.).

Central Complex is a mixed lithodemic unit of Rank 3 composed of largely intrusive rocks with screens and irregular masses of associated extrusive rocks and country rocks, commonly but not necessarily arranged spatially around one or more focal points; a central complex can encompass several centres; at present, central complexes defined in the UK are generally considered to represent the roots of a central volcano at a relatively shallow crustal level - such an association is not necessarily implied by the definition proposed here. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Centre is a lithodemic unit of Rank 4, grouping lithodemic units classified at Rank 6 and/or 5 that are focused tightly around a central point, and usually intersecting, of similar age and common origin. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Class (artificial, rank 1) is a unit of Rank 1 in the BGS framework for classifying artificial (man-made) ground (Ford, J, Kessler, H, Cooper, A H, Price, S J and Humpage, A J. 2010. An enhanced classification for artificial ground. British Geological Survey Open Report, OR/10/036. 32pp.).

Cluster is a lithodemic unit of Rank 4, grouping lithodemic units classified at Rank 6 and/or 5 that are associated spatially but not focused tightly, i.e. they are too scattered to be classified as a centre; a cluster may, for example, consist of two dyke-swarms, a sill-swarm and numerous pipes, scattered over a wide area. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Complex is an assemblage of rocks consisting of a mixture of lithodemic and lithostratigraphical units, or of intrusive, highly metamorphosed and/or highly deformed lithodemic units, with or without highly complicated structure. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.), and mixed-class units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.).

Cone-sheet is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of a sheet with a cone shape that dips inwards towards a central focal point. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Cone-sheet-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of cone-sheets. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Diatreme is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of a breccia-filled volcanic pipe inferred to have been formed by gaseous disruption. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Diatreme-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of diatremes. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Dyke is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of a sheet of igneous rock emplaced along a steep, generally near-vertical fracture; normally discordant to the structure of its host rocks. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Dyke-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of dykes. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Flow is the smallest formal unit in the hierarchy of volcanic flow deposits. Flow names may be applied to distinctive extrusive rock bodies, distinguished by texture, composition, or other criteria. This term forms part of the internationally accepted framework for classifying lithostratigraphical units, and is equivalent in rank to a bed (North American Commission on Stratigraphic Nomenclature. 2004. North American Stratigraphic Code. AAPG Bulletin, Vol. 89, No. 11, pp. 1547-1591).

Formation is the primary formal unit of lithostratigraphical classification used to map, describe, and interpret the geology of a region. A formation is generally defined as the smallest mappable unit and has lithological characteristics that distinguish it from adjacent formations. A formation is defined by a type section (stratotype) or by type area. Where possible, the top and base should be defined but it is recognised that the nature of these boundaries and the bounding deposits may vary laterally. This term forms part of the internationally accepted framework for classifying lithostratigraphical units, and has Rank 4 (McMillan, A A, Hamblin, R J O and Merritt, J W. 2011. A lithostratigraphical framework for onshore Quaternary and Neogene (Tertiary) superficial deposits of Great Britain and the Isle of Man. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/10/03. 343pp.).

Group is the formal lithostratigraphical unit next in rank above a formation and is commonly applied to a sequence of contiguous formations with significant diagnostic lithological characteristics. This term forms part of the internationally accepted framework for classifying lithostratigraphical units, and has Rank 2 (McMillan, A A, Hamblin, R J O and Merritt, J W. 2011. A lithostratigraphical framework for onshore Quaternary and Neogene (Tertiary) superficial deposits of Great Britain and the Isle of Man. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/10/03. 343pp.).

Intrusion is a unit of geological material produced by an intrusive process and bounded by observed or inferred intrusive margins; usually used to refer to any unit of rock or magma formed by emplacement of magma and/or pyroclastic material into the subsurface, however units of non-igneous material can also result from an intrusive process, e.g. salt 'domes'; the term may be used formally (with a capital 'I') for a lithodemic unit of Rank 6, or informally (with a small 'i') to refer to any intrusive lithodemic unit(s). This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Intrusion-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of intrusions. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Intrusive-complex is not an approved term in the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Laccolith is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of an intrusion that is roughly circular in plan, concordant with the structure of the country rock, and generally has a planar floor and a domed roof. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Laccolith-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of laccoliths. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Layer is a volume of rock that is, or was formerly, essentially tabular, and is bounded by broadly parallel surfaces of tectonic or uncertain origin; also a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 6 with these characteristics. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.).

Lens is a lensoid body of rock bounded by converging, generally curved surfaces of tectonic or uncertain origin; also a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 6 with these characteristics. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.).

Litho-morpho-genetic unit is an informal, generic type of superficial deposit defined and identified primarily on its lithology, morphology, genesis or some combination of these; sometimes with geographic or age qualifiers but no lithostratigraphical name. Examples include peat; tidal flat deposit; alluvium; river terrace deposit; blown sand; till.
Litho-morpho-genetic unit at rank 1.
Litho-morpho-genetic unit at rank 2.
Litho-morpho-genetic unit at rank 3.
Litho-morpho-genetic unit at rank 4.
Litho-morpho-genetic unit at rank 5.
Litho-morpho-genetic unit at rank 6.

Lithodeme is defined in the North American Stratigraphic Code as "a body of intrusive, pervasively deformed, or highly metamorphosed rock, generally non-tabular and lacking primary depositional structures, and characterised by lithic homogeneity"; the NASC regards 'lithodeme' as the fundamental unit in lithodemic classification, broadly equivalent to the lithostratigraphical term 'formation'; the term lithodeme has not been adopted by BGS because it is considered too broadly defined (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.); the term lithodemic unit is preferred for all units encompassed by the NASC definition of lithodeme, and for groups of such units at higher lithodemic ranks.

Lopolith is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a body of kilometre-scale or larger that is concordant, broadly saucer-shaped and typically layered; a 'simple' lopolith consists of essentially one intrusion, whereas a 'composite' lopolith consists of two or more; the intrusions in composite lopoliths are inferred to be related genetically, and to be associated spatially because the magma batches used a common pathway through the crust. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Mass is a body of rock of irregular or unspecified shape, bounded by surfaces of tectonic or uncertain origin; also a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 6 with these characteristics. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.).

Member is the formal lithostratigraphical unit next in rank below a formation and is always part of a formation. Formations need not be divided either wholly or partially into members. A member may extend from one formation to another. This term forms part of the internationally accepted framework for classifying lithostratigraphical units, and has Rank 5 (McMillan, A A, Hamblin, R J O and Merritt, J W. 2011. A lithostratigraphical framework for onshore Quaternary and Neogene (Tertiary) superficial deposits of Great Britain and the Isle of Man. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/10/03. 343pp.).

Neck is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of the feeder 'pipe' of a volcano, which has been infilled with collapsed material from the surface vent and commonly intruded by magma, after eruption has ceased, to form a plug; exposed due to subsequent erosion. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.). See also: vent.

Neck-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of necks. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Ophiolite-complex is a mixed lithodemic unit of Rank 3 composed of ophiolite (a section or sections of the oceanic crust, with or without the subjacent upper mantle) that has been uplifted or emplaced to be exposed within continental crustal rocks, during which process the ophiolite becomes tectonically 'mixed' (usually interleaved) with crustal rocks; strictly speaking, an ophiolite-complex is a structural unit composed in part of intrusive rock; it is included in the BGS framework for classifying intrusive lithodemic units because some ophiolite-complexes consist largely of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Package is a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 4 uniting two or more tectono-metamorphic units of lower rank that display a natural association and are largely or wholly contiguous at outcrop. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.). See also: set.

Pipe is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of a discordant, cylindrical intrusion, normally steeply orientated. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Pipe-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of pipes. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Plug is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of the solidified remains of a cylindrical intrusion of magma, inferred to be intrusive into or associated with a volcanic neck. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Plug-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of plugs. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Pluton is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a body of intrusive rock, generally with a simple, regular margin, the whole being kilometre-scale or larger and with a cylindrical, lenticular or tabular shape; a 'simple' pluton consists of essentially one intrusion, whereas a 'composite' pluton consists of two or more; the intrusions in composite igneous plutons are inferred to be related genetically, and to be associated spatially because the magma batches used a common pathway through the crust. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Province is a region encompassing all igneous units (lithodemic and lithostratigraphical) related to a major tectonothermal event (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.). See also: superprovince.

Ring-complex is a mixed lithodemic unit of Rank 4 composed of one or more ring-intrusions, ring-dykes, cone-sheets, ring-swarms and cone-sheet-swarms, with their country-rocks. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Ring-dyke is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of a sheet that is arcuate or annular in plan, and usually vertical or inclined steeply outwards. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Ring-intrusion is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of an intrusion observed or inferred to have been emplaced within, or bounded by, a ring-fracture. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Ring-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of ring-dykes with or without cone-sheets. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Set is a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 4 uniting two or more tectono-metamorphic units of lower rank that display a natural association and are dispersed (not contiguous) at outcrop. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.). See also: package.

Sheet is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of an intrusion with broadly parallel margins and one dimension much shorter than the other two; most sheets have a broadly tabular shape, but they may be curved, sinuous or irregular. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Sheet-complex is a mixed lithodemic unit of Rank 4 composed of a sheet-swarm and its country-rocks. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Sheet-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of sheets. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Sill is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of a sheet of igneous rock emplaced along a near-horizontal fracture; usually broadly concordant in stratified rocks. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Sill-complex is a mixed lithodemic unit of Rank 4 composed of a sill-swarm and its country-rocks. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Sill-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of sills. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Subassemblage is a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 3 uniting a subset of the units within an assemblage that display a natural association. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.).

Subgroup is not in the formal lithostratigraphical hierarchy, but exceptionally, a group may be divided into subgroups. The term has Rank 3 in the lithostratigraphical hierarchy (McMillan, A A, Hamblin, R J O and Merritt, J W. 2011. A lithostratigraphical framework for onshore Quaternary and Neogene (Tertiary) superficial deposits of Great Britain and the Isle of Man. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/10/03. 343pp.).
Subsuccession is not an approved term in the BGS framework for classifying lithostratigraphical or lithodemic units.

Subsuite is a lithodemic unit of Rank 3 grouping two or more lithodemic units from a single suite that share some similarities in a meaningful combination of observed features; the lithodemic unit next lower in rank to suite. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Subswarm is an informal unit grouping two or more intrusions that are part of a formally classified swarm but are distinguished by location, composition or some other geological feature(s); it is emphasised that subswarms must be informal, and cannot form part of a formal lithodemic classification; as such, the term should be used sparingly (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).
Succession is not an approved term in the BGS framework for classifying lithostratigraphical or lithodemic units.

Suite is a lithodemic unit of Rank 2 grouping two or more lithodemic units of lower rank (i.e. ranks 3 to 6), and of the same class (intrusive igneous, highly metamorphosed, highly deformed or mixed), that display a degree of natural relationship through similarities in a meaningful combination of observed features such as shape, spatial distribution, composition, and age; mixed lithodemic units composed mainly of intrusive igneous rock may be included in a suite otherwise grouping intrusive units; the lithodemic unit next lower in rank to supersuite. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Superassemblage is a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 1 uniting two or more tectono-metamorphic units that are of lower rank and display a natural association. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.).

Supergroup may be used for several associated groups or for associated formations and groups with significant lithological properties in common. This term forms part of the internationally accepted framework for classifying lithostratigraphical units, and has Rank 1 (McMillan, A A, Hamblin, R J O and Merritt, J W. 2011. A lithostratigraphical framework for onshore Quaternary and Neogene (Tertiary) superficial deposits of Great Britain and the Isle of Man. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/10/03. 343pp.).

Superprovince is a group of two or more provinces that are related to a major tectonothermal event (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).
Supersuccession is not an approved term in the BGS framework for classifying lithostratigraphical or lithodemic units.

Supersuite is a lithodemic unit of Rank 1 grouping two or more suites that have a degree of natural relationship to one another; supersuites may also contain lithodemic units that are not assigned to suites; the highest ranking formal lithodemic unit. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Swarm is a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 5 uniting two or more tectono-metamorphic units of Rank 6 that display a natural association and are dispersed (not contiguous) at outcrop; a term from Rank 6 of the tectono-metamorphic units hierarchy may be used to qualify the type of swarm, e.g. layer-swarm. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.). See also: train.

Train is a tectono-metamorphic unit of Rank 5 uniting two or more tectono-metamorphic units of Rank 6 that display a natural association and have a dispersed but broadly linear spatial arrangement at outcrop. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying tectono-metamorphic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.). See also: swarm.

Type (artificial, rank 2) is a unit of Rank 2 in the BGS framework for classifying artificial (man-made) ground (Ford, J, Kessler, H, Cooper, A H, Price, S J and Humpage, A J. 2010. An enhanced classification for artificial ground. British Geological Survey Open Report, OR/10/036. 32pp.).

Unclassified is used for terms that do not fit into the BGS frameworks for classifying lithostratigraphical, lithodemic or artificial deposits. These include informal terms without rank, and composite terms representing two or more geological units used on BGS geological maps.

Unit (artificial, rank 3) is a unit of Rank 3 in the BGS framework for classifying artificial (man-made) ground (Ford, J, Kessler, H, Cooper, A H, Price, S J and Humpage, A J. 2010. An enhanced classification for artificial ground. British Geological Survey Open Report, OR/10/036. 32pp.).

Unit (tectono-metamorphic) is not an approved term in the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.).

Vein is a lithodemic unit of Rank 6 composed of a sheet-like body that is generally narrower and more irregular than features classified as sills, dykes or sheets; the term is also used for features that are not lithodemic units, e.g. the mineral filling in, or replacement around, a fracture. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Vein-complex is a mixed lithodemic unit of Rank 4 composed of a vein-swarm and its country-rocks, the whole being typically intermediate in character between a xenolith-rich pluton and veined country-rock. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Vein-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of veins, typically with an irregular disposition. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Vent is, strictly, an opening at the Earth’s surface through which volcanic material is extruded; on UK maps a vent usually represents the chaotic near-surface deposits formed by collapse of the original crater; a lithodemic unit of Rank 6. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.). See also: neck.
Vent or Neck. See also: neck, vent.

Vent-swarm is a lithodemic unit of Rank 5 composed of a swarm of vents. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Vent-system is not an approved term in the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Volcano-complex is a mixed lithodemic unit of Rank 3 composed of extrusions, related intrusions and volcaniclastic products, at a site of persistent volcanic activity. This term forms part of the BGS framework for classifying lithodemic units composed entirely or predominantly of intrusive rock (Gillespie, M R, Stephenson, D and Millward, D. 2008. BGS classification of lithodemic units: Proposals for classifying units of intrusive rock. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/08/05. 31pp.).

Zone (igneous, metamorphic, tectonic) is a volume or area of geological material in which the frequency of a feature, or the degree to which a particular state or condition is developed, is measurably higher than in the background (Leslie, A G, Krabbendam, M and Gillespie, M R. 2012. BGS classification of lithodemic units: proposals for classifying tectonometamorphic units and mixed-class units. British Geological Survey Research Report, RR/12/02. 35pp.).
